authorityBoundary: This crosswalk expresses PALO design fit and governance routing. It does not establish equivalence, implementation effectiveness, OWASP endorsement, compliance, certification, or production authorization.

ratingScale.direct: A first-class PALO artifact or control materially addresses the risk within the stated route.
ratingScale.supporting: PALO contributes governance or containment, but risk-specific technical safeguards remain necessary.
ratingScale.gap: The current route has no specific coverage for the risk's main technical mechanism.

routes.label: PALO Framework
routes.role: Lifecycle governance, accountable ownership, controls, evidence, monitoring and review.

routes.label: PALO-AM
routes.role: Agent identity, authority, autonomy, tool boundaries, oversight and circuit breakers.

routes.label: PALO-AI
routes.role: Exact claims, policy, approval, one-time capability, execution receipt and outcome verification.

summary.overallFit: Strong governance fit with incomplete technical resolution. PALO routes all ten risks, but LLM09 and LLM10 need targeted control-library and runtime extensions.

risks.title: Prompt Injection
risks.verdict: Contain the consequence; do not promise complete prompt-injection prevention.
risks.paloResponse: PALO treats the model as untrusted, requires adversarial testing and meaningful review, and uses PALO-AM and PALO-AI to constrain authority through deterministic policy, approval and one-time execution capabilities.
externalSafeguards: Adaptive red-team testing with the defense disclosed
reopenTriggers: New tool or external communication path

risks.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
risks.verdict: Govern the data surface and evidence, but add dedicated privacy and data-security controls.
risks.paloResponse: PALO provides data provenance, change control, adversarial testing and incident handling. PALO-AM can narrow tool access and data clearance, while PALO-AI can bind selected actions, but neither replaces retrieval authorization or DLP.
risks.accountableOwner: Data Owner and Privacy or Security Owner

risks.title: Excessive Agency
risks.verdict: This is the strongest PALO fit, provided the governed path cannot be bypassed.
risks.paloResponse: PALO-AM defines identity, authority, autonomy, minimum tools, oversight and reversibility. PALO-AI can bind an exact action to policy, approval, a one-time capability, an execution receipt and post-state verification.
externalSafeguards: Production workload identity and principal-level RBAC
Removal of alternate privileged execution paths
Independently assessed connectors and policy distribution
risks.accountableOwner: Accountable System Owner and IAM or Security Owner

risks.title: Supply Chain
risks.verdict: PALO governs supplier and change decisions; artifact integrity remains a dedicated engineering duty.
risks.paloResponse: PALO supplier due diligence, data provenance and material-change gates create accountable promotion decisions. PALO-AM inventories agent tools, while PALO-AI registers executors and verifiers but does not yet attest the complete supply chain.
risks.accountableOwner: Supplier Risk and ML Platform Owner

risks.title: Data and Model Poisoning
risks.verdict: PALO can govern integrity decisions, but current PALO-AI does not detect poisoning.
risks.paloResponse: PALO provides provenance, change gates, adversarial testing, incident response and rollback governance. PALO-AM adds memory lifecycle and authority boundaries, but poisoning detection and model-pipeline integrity remain external. Boundary: LLM05 owns persistent corruption of source, chunk, training or embedding-model inputs; LLM09 owns attacks that require embedding geometry, similarity ranking, collision, inference or inversion.
externalSafeguards: Dataset and model lineage with signatures
Ingestion validation, source authentication and trust boundaries
Persistent RAG corpus and embedding-model poisoning detection
minimumEvidence: Persistent corpus poisoning and retrieval-impact test
risks.accountableOwner: Data or Model Owner and MLOps Owner

risks.title: Unbounded Consumption
risks.verdict: PALO-AM supplies the governance pattern; production runtime budgets are not yet delivered by PALO-AI.
risks.paloResponse: PALO-AM requires bounded action space, circuit breakers, abort conditions and monitoring. PALO can assign thresholds and escalation ownership, but PALO-AI lists rate limiting and abuse controls as production-readiness gaps.
externalSafeguards: Token, action, time and cost caps
Per-principal rate limits and hard spending ceilings
risks.accountableOwner: Platform or SRE and FinOps Owner

risks.title: Misinformation
risks.verdict: PALO can prevent unverified claims from silently becoming high-impact actions; it cannot guarantee truth.
risks.paloResponse: PALO connects current sources, claims, review and decision evidence. PALO-AM separates recommendation from authority, while PALO-AI can verify authoritative post-state against an Effect Contract after a governed action.
externalSafeguards: Calibrated human review for consequential claims
minimumEvidence: Outcome attestation with stated causal limits

risks.title: Hidden Context Exposure
risks.verdict: Move secrets and authority outside the model context; do not rely on hidden prompts as controls.
risks.paloResponse: PALO-AM treats the model as an untrusted reasoning engine and requires deterministic authorization. PALO-AI keeps policy, approval and execution authority in the control path rather than in prompt instructions.

risks.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
risks.verdict: This is a targeted PALO extension area; current governance controls do not secure the vector layer by themselves.
risks.paloResponse: PALO data provenance, adversarial testing and incident response provide the governance shell. PALO-AM can restrict who and what may query tools, but current PALO-AI has no vector-store enforcement or embedding lifecycle control. Boundary: LLM09 owns attacks that depend on embedding geometry, similarity ranking, threshold collision, membership inference or inversion; persistent source or chunk corruption is handed to the LLM05 owner.
externalSafeguards: Deletion reconciliation and encrypted backups treated at source-data sensitivity
Embedding inversion resistance assessment and source-leak incident classification
Ingest, retrieval and ranking anomaly detection
minimumEvidence: Pre-retrieval chunk-level authorization and tenant-isolation test
Quantified embedding-inversion test using Vec2Text, ZSInvert, Zero2Text or a threat-model-equivalent technique
Adversarial-query retrieval-evasion, similarity-collision and threshold-straddling test results
Vector-layer poisoning and ranking-manipulation test with an explicit LLM05 handoff for persistent corpus corruption
Tamper-evident retrieval trace and residual-risk decision
risks.accountableOwner: Vector Store Owner and Product Security
reopenTriggers: Vector leak, inversion result or retrieval anomaly

risks.title: Improper Output Handling
risks.verdict: PALO can gate actions and evidence decisions, but sink-safe output handling needs an explicit extension.
risks.paloResponse: PALO adversarial testing and PALO-AM tool-schema controls reduce unsafe propagation. PALO-AI validates governance contracts and exact action claims, not every generated HTML, SQL, shell, terminal, email or code sink.
externalSafeguards: Outbound fetch restrictions and generated-code security tests
risks.accountableOwner: Application Security and Downstream Sink Owner

governance.applicabilityRule: Use this LLM Top 10 when the model is an application component. Pair it with the OWASP Agentic Top 10 and apply PALO-AM and PALO-AI when tools, persistent memory, multi-step planning or autonomous action are present.
reopenTriggers: Material architecture, tool, memory or data-scope change
